project.name: Ableton Project Setup
project.description: Automated Ableton Live project builder — takes raw stems, classifies them, detects BPM, and creates a fully laid-out .als file matching Sam's mixing workflow.
project.location: Wired Masters Dropbox/Sam Wills/0.1---GIT HUB---/Ableton Project Setup/

Source/project_builder.py.purpose: Main orchestrator: scans stem folders, classifies stems, detects BPM, copies audio, builds flat references, detects group buses, and patches the final ALS.
Source/project_builder.py.notes: Contains single-version and multi-version build paths. As of 2026-06-26 it can call audio_ml_classify.py for filename-unknown stems. Multi-version later stacks are placed on phrase slots, then nudged together by the earliest credible kick-named layer. Since 2026-07-02: apply_ableton_folder_icon() gives built projects the Ableton folder icon (Desktop.ini + AProject.ico, Windows-only, never fails a build); reports (Session Report + ML Classification Report) write into a Reports/ subfolder via _reports_dir()/session_report_path() instead of the project root. 2026-07-06/08: _resolve_project_bpm() treats a filename BPM as a hint verified against the audio (never authoritative); _safe_filename() sanitises user-typed names; _make_project_context()/_patch_and_validate()/_finish_project() are the shared head/tail extracted from both build paths in the M1 refactor (see Documentation/M1_REFACTOR_PLAN.md, complete) — multi-version now has parity with single for silent-stem parking, wet/dry dry-park, and updated-stem matching.

Source/stem_classifier.py.purpose: Filename-based classification and display track-name generation.
Source/stem_classifier.py.notes: Patterns cover drums, bass, music, vocals, FX, sends, references, and common messy export names. classify_stems() walks the folder DEPTH-FIRST to any depth (2026-07-13, A4) so a format-wrapper pack (Drums/24bit WAV/Kick.wav) no longer builds empty; one-level order is byte-identical to the old scan; skips __MACOSX/dotfile/output folders via versions.is_skip_dir. Since 2026-07-02: FX_STRONG_PATTERNS (downer/sub-drop/riser/uplifter) outranks bass/music so transition FX don't get grabbed by instrument words; hook/topline are guarded weak vocal signals (stripped, then checked against remaining instrument/drum/FX words) so 'Hook Main' -> vocals but 'Synth Hook'/'Guitar Topline' stay music.

Source/audio_ml_classify.py.purpose: Heavy audio-content classifier for unnamed stems using Demucs source bins and optional Whisper vocal confirmation.
Source/audio_ml_classify.py.notes: Used for the Moby unnamed-stem test. Runs as a subprocess from project_builder.py so ML failures do not abort the build.

Source/stem_analysis.py.purpose: Numpy audio analysis for full-mix/reference detection and group-bus/submix detection.
Source/stem_analysis.py.notes: Keeps full mixes and detected buses out of the flat-reference sum.

Source/als_patcher.py.purpose: Raw-text ALS patching engine for tracks, clips, groups, locators, routing, colours, and regions.
Source/als_patcher.py.notes: Do not replace with XML libraries; Ableton is sensitive to formatting. Since 2026-07-02: find_audio_regions(return_peak=True) returns TRUE PEAK (loudest single sample), not windowed RMS, so a sparse-but-real stem (quiet shaker) isn't false-flagged as silent; SILENCE_FLOOR_DB is -66 dBFS under the new semantics (both numpy and stdlib paths compute true peak, verified to agree).

Source/bpm_detector.py.purpose: BPM detection from kick/drum onsets, with optional Kick Detector V3 CRNN onset picking.
Source/bpm_detector.py.notes: Returns both folded grid phase and first_actual_onset_sec so multi-version alignment can use the physical timing anchor. As of 2026-07-09, detect_bpm can lazy-call the sibling Kick Detector repo's Source/infer.py::KickModel with Models/kick_crnn_V3.pt and feed those onsets into the existing lattice fit; the pure-stdlib energy onset picker remains default/fallback. On STUDIO-2 the local gitignored Config/project_builder.json enables V3 through subprocess mode via py -3.14 because the Project Setup Python 3.13 runtime lacks librosa.

Source/bounce.py.purpose: Flat-reference WAV summing with numpy fast path and stdlib fallback.
Source/bounce.py.notes: Used to print one red FLAT REF track rather than duplicating stems into a reference group.

Source/subgroup_cluster.py.purpose: Clusters a working category's stems into nested sub-groups by filename tokens (singer-first for vocals; Kit/Percussion for drums; instrument family for music).
Source/subgroup_cluster.py.notes: Returns the category's stems reordered + tagged with subgroup_key/name/color, or None when no useful sub-grouping applies. A sub-group needs 2+ members; conservative on drums/music. Consumed by project_builder._apply_subgroups; rendered as nested GroupTracks by als_patcher._apply_track_groups.

Source/versions.py.purpose: Detects alternate-version subfolders/name-tokens by mirrored element keys; pairs elements across versions.
Source/versions.py.notes: Scans are nest-aware (2026-07-13, A4): _audio_here() = direct children only (the shallow top-level-stem test), _audio_under() = recursive (sees a version behind a format wrapper Extended/WAV/...) but excludes __MACOSX/dotfile/output folders AND special ref/update branches (a nested REF/ is gathered by project_builder, not counted as a version member). is_skip_dir() is the shared skip predicate (macOS junk, dotfiles, tool output folders Reports/Ableton Project Info/MASTER RENDERS/Backup). element_key() strips a trailing export index before pairing (2026-07-06). sorted_element_key() is an order-independent fallback (consulted only when element_key misses) that pairs a reversed-word-order element like FX_FILLS/FILLS_FX across versions. dry_pair_key() is a wet/dry-stripped order-independent key for pairing dry vocal parks across versions (element_key alone collides every _DRY stem to 'dry').

Source/validate_project.py.purpose: Canonical generated-project validator for ALS gzip/XML readability, tempo, tempo automation, Session Time, refs, FLAT REF, and file refs.
Source/validate_project.py.notes: Use this instead of verify_output.py for arbitrary outputs.

Config/project_builder.json.purpose: Local defaults for template path, output base, ML interpreter, and ML enablement.

sessions.summary: A4 deep-nesting/format-wrapper support (audit A4, previously deferred). Proved on synthetic packs that classify_stems AND detect_versions both scanned only ONE subfolder level, so a pack nesting stems under a format wrapper (Drums/24bit WAV/Kick.wav, or Extended/WAV/... + Radio/WAV/...) built a COMPLETELY EMPTY project with no flag, and partial nesting silently dropped the deep stems. Fix (Codex plan-reviewed -> SOUND WITH CHANGES, all 3 findings folded in): (A1) versions.py splits the old one-level _audio_in into _audio_here (shallow, the top-level-stem test) + _audio_under (recursive, excludes __MACOSX/dotfile/output folders AND special ref/update branches so a nested REF/ isn't a false version member); (A2) classify_stems is now a sorted depth-first walk whose one-level order is byte-identical to the old scan; (A3) _extract_special_dirs is ancestor-aware; (Part B) a single-path coverage backstop (independent recursive manifest vs claimed -> any leftover parked as a reference + flagged) + a hard guard (audio present but zero working stems -> loud ValueError, never a silent empty build); plus collision-safe copies (_copy_stem_dest) so two deep stems sharing a basename don't overwrite each other. Shared helpers versions.is_skip_dir + project_builder._all_source_audio. Validated: m1_refactor_harness compare -> Admonic(single)+Fallon(multi) rebuild byte-identical .als XML + report (no regression); new Tests/test_deep_nesting.py 9/9 (incl. an e2e format-wrapper build that validate_project PASSes, the hard guard, collision-safe copy); full suite 26/26. decisions.decision: ALS files are patched as raw text lines, not via XML libraries.
decisions.why: Ableton's parser is strict about whitespace, attribute order, and line endings. xml.etree.ElementTree corrupts the format. See ABLETON_INTERACTION.md.

decisions.decision: Stems are placed unwarped (IsWarped=false). BPM detected from kick/snare sets global tempo.
decisions.why: Sam's stems arrive pre-rendered at the correct BPM. No time-stretching needed.

decisions.decision: Flat reference is always our own bounce (sum of mix stems), never a supplied 'ref'/'riff'/master file. Single track at the bottom, color 14 (red), muted, routed to Ext. Out. Supplied references kept as separate match tracks (also red). No GroupTrack.
decisions.why: A supplied ref file can't be trusted to equal the stem sum (may be another artist's track or a limited master); verifying it would require bouncing the sum anyway, so always print our own. Single track + Ext. Out bypasses the master chain and retires the long-standing 'ref group opens expanded' bug.

decisions.decision: Group-bus / sub-mix stems (a bus left among individual stems) are detected via find_group_buses() in stem_analysis.py: stems are sample-aligned, so a bus is the sum of its members; a non-negative greedy matching pursuit (Gram-matrix space) flags any stem reconstructed >88% by a positive sum of >=2 others. Buses are parked muted/grey (37) at the very bottom below refs, kept for recall, and excluded from the flat-ref sum. Non-negativity flags the bus, never its members.
decisions.why: Sam: this is a big, frequent problem on real packs — a producer leaves a group bus among the stems, you press play and everything sounds wrong (double-counted), then have to hunt for which stem is the bus. Filenames/spectra can't distinguish a bus from a stem, but the sample-aligned sum relationship can. Validated: caught Coldabank 'All Drums' + Far Away 'BASS EGYBE' (=b+b_3) with no false positives.

decisions.decision: Ambiguous stems get an audio-content check (Source/stem_analysis.py, numpy FFT): a file filenames can't place that reads as a full mix (crest<=5 + 6+ bands + sustain>=0.6) is moved to references so it's never summed into the flat bounce. Approach borrowed from Loudness Leveller (band energy) + Automated DJ Mixes (low-end) but implemented numpy-only (no librosa/ffmpeg); filename-only fallback if numpy absent. Audio kick-detection was tried and dropped — kick vs bass overlap too much on aggregate spectral features; filenames (incl. 'K') handle kicks.
decisions.why: A test batch of 5 random finished mixes showed cryptically-named full mixes ('Current', 'TEST MIX') being summed into the flat ref and polluting it (Far Away peaked 3.85). Filenames are unreliable on messy real packs; audio content is the robust signal. Crest factor (compression) is the key full-mix discriminator, tuned/validated on labelled real files.

decisions.decision: bounce.py uses numpy when installed (optional import) with a pure-stdlib fallback; both paths verified bit-identical. Working groups coloured with the category colour; group names Drums/Bass/Music/Vox/FX (bass IS grouped per Sam 2026-06-25). Reference tracks coloured red (14). Silence trim retuned tighter (headroom 55dB / window 0.1s / min-gap 2.5s / tail 1s) so clips hug audio without chopping decays.
decisions.why: Optional numpy keeps the tool install-free yet ~15x faster where numpy exists. Category-coloured group headers read at a glance. Sam asked for red refs, bass grouping, and tighter silence trimming after seeing the first demo.

decisions.decision: Filename-unknown stems can be classified with an optional heavy ML second stage: Demucs energy bins map to drums/bass/music/vocals and Whisper confirms likely vocals.
decisions.why: The Moby test pack intentionally used generic names such as Audio 10_02.wav. Filename rules alone would collapse most tracks into Music; source-bin classification gives a better first-pass project while preserving a human-readable report for review.

decisions.decision: Multi-version later sections are placed as a whole stack on the next phrase slot, then the entire stack is nudged together using the earliest credible kick-named layer as the grid anchor.
decisions.why: Radio edits can have no dry kick at the start. Fallon proved that anchoring to the dry kick or to the locator is wrong; the musical stack must stay locked together and only receive the small left/right nudge Sam would do by eye in Ableton.

decisions.decision: A filename-labelled BPM is a HINT, not authoritative -- it's grid-checked against the audio, which is the arbiter. On a conflict the tool uses the audio-detected tempo and raises a flag (never silently keeps the wrong label, never hard-stops).
decisions.why: Sam's Cole Horton pack had stems tagged '130BPM' but the track was really 132 -- the old code trusted the label outright and never even ran the detector.

decisions.decision: M1 refactor extracts the shared HEAD (_make_project_context) and TAIL (_patch_and_validate/_finish_project) from the single- and multi-version build paths, but keeps the two middle LAYOUT logics separate (single=one timeline, multi=versions stacked on shared tracks) rather than forcing a full pv-based unification.
decisions.why: A full unification would drag Fallon's version-stack alignment model into simple single-version builds and risk subtly changing behaviour Sam relies on daily; the audit's actual complaint (duplicated logic silently drifting apart) is fixed by sharing the head/tail and closing the three real parity gaps (silent/wet-dry/updated-stem), which a 3-brain review (Codex+MiniMax) confirmed was the right scope.
